Since I'm having trouble with the search tools, I'll use my knowledge to evaluate each statement:

Statement A: "They are found in nature in certain plants"
This is true. Oxalates are naturally occurring compounds found in many plants including spinach, rhubarb, sorrel, and many leafy greens. Plants produce oxalic acid as part of their normal metabolism, and this forms oxalates when combined with minerals like calcium.

Statement B: "They are used in rust and ink stain removers"
This is true. Oxalic acid and oxalates are common ingredients in commercial rust removers and stain removers, particularly for ink stains. Their acidic properties help dissolve metal oxides (rust) and break down certain types of stains.

Statement C: "They can clog kidney tubules"
This is true. When oxalates bind with calcium in the kidneys, they can form calcium oxalate crystals which are the most common component of kidney stones. These crystals can accumulate and clog kidney tubules, leading to kidney stones and potential kidney damage.

Based on my analysis, all three statements about oxalates are true.
